newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary electricity corp MVM sell-off seen delayed.
newsitem.headline: Hungary electricity corp MVM sell-off seen delayed.

text.p: Hungary is likely to sell stakes in the national electricity supplier MVM and bus maker Ikarus only at the very end of its privatisation programme, Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha said on Tuesday.
Hungary plans to complete the privatisation programme, which began in the late 1980s, in 1998.
Csiha told a news conference that a planned amendment to the privatisation law would reduce the value of assets to be retained by the state by 20-30 billion forints from 340 billion.

She added that further assets of 60-100 billion were unlikely to be sold by the end of the privatisation programme either on the lack of investor interest or because preparations for a sell-off would not be complete.
"In my view, for example MVM and Ikarus belong in this category," she said. "For these companies preparations must should be made which will take many more months."
The minister did not make clear when MVM's privatisation could be expected.

The state privatisation agency APV had said earlier that MVM's privatisation would probably not happen this year as questions such as the conversion of earlier assets and long-distance electricity transfer remained unsolved.
According to the government's plans, Hungary would sell a minority stake in the MVM group, which includes the country's only nuclear power plant, Paks, Csiha said.
